artifacts.memo:
# Product decision memo — owner approved

**Prioritize a test restoring basic playback controls for free users.** The issue is users being forced to shuffle, unable to go back, seek, repeat, play in order or pick a song, and encountering skip limits. One review puts it plainly: “to play in order buy premium” ([review 7e271329](phase7-cohort-spotcheck-v3.md)). The cohort is named **Free-tier playback controls locked behind Premium**; some restrictions are inferred rather than explicitly attributed to Premium.

**Why this issue.** Other—unspecified ranks first under the contract’s severity-sum rule, with 36,225 reviews ([B1](phase7/claims.csv), [S10](phase7/secondary-claims.csv)). It represents general dissatisfaction with no stated cause, so it is not a specific fix target. Controls rank second in both the propagated baseline and random-prefix-only view ([S1](phase7/secondary-claims.csv), [S2](phase7/secondary-claims.csv)).

Controls barely change between views: **4,444 reviews / 13,877 severity points** in the baseline ([B2](phase7/claims.csv), [B3](phase7/claims.csv)), versus **4,440 / 13,865** in the random prefix ([S3](phase7/secondary-claims.csv), [S4](phase7/secondary-claims.csv)). Ads fall from **6,037 / 12,965** ([B4](phase7/claims.csv), [B5](phase7/claims.csv)) to **4,088 / 9,071** ([S5](phase7/secondary-claims.csv), [S6](phase7/secondary-claims.csv)). Exact-text propagation gives repeated short complaints such as “Too many ads” additional weight by copying their labels to matching rows outside the prefix. In the seeded random sample, controls carry approximately **1.5×** the severity-weighted complaints of ads ([S7](phase7/secondary-claims.csv)). Baseline mean severity is approximately **3.1 for controls versus 2.1 for ads** ([B6](phase7/claims.csv), [B7](phase7/claims.csv)).

Absolute counts cover only classified rows. The random prefix is a uniform sample of all nonempty reviews, so its proportions are the best estimate of the full mix; the baseline adds 1,949 additional ad rows ([S11](phase7/secondary-claims.csv)) but only 4 controls rows ([S12](phase7/secondary-claims.csv)). Remaining uncertainty comes from sampling error and lexical grouping, not the direction of this comparison.

**Proposed next step.** Test restoring back, seek and repeat for a subset of free users. Measure complaint rates, one-star rating rates and Premium conversion against a comparison group, using predefined observation windows and decision criteria. These controls appear to be used as upgrade incentives, so the test should weigh any change in Premium conversion against the reduction in complaints. An alternative is an ad-frequency cap. These are proposed experiments, not claims of causal impact, revenue gains or reduced churn.

**Decision limits.** Completed labels cover approximately **36% of nonempty rows** ([S8](phase7/secondary-claims.csv)); approximately **65% of classified complaint/cancellation rows have no specific cause assigned** ([S9](phase7/secondary-claims.csv)). Grouping uses final, spot-checked lexical rules (v3), which can misassign or miss reviews. Verifier agreement is not human accuracy; the verifier and fallback share the same model.

*Evidence key: B references are checker-compatible baseline claims; S references are separately documented secondary analyses, not baseline claims. Engineering provenance and unavailable-usage disclosures are in the README. Owner-approved revision of the saved model draft.*

alternatives: Investigate intrusive or frequent advertisements as the next specific actionable alternative; it ranks below the recommended issue in the baseline and below it in the random-prefix ranking. [usability--ad-interruptions:rank] [sample:usability--ad-interruptions:rank]

Unspecified usability complaints are another alternative but do not identify a concrete defect; their relative position versus advertisements changes in the random-prefix ranking. [usability--unspecified:rank] [sample:usability--unspecified:rank] [usability--ad-interruptions:rank] [sample:usability--ad-interruptions:rank]
Premium subscription and upgrade complaints rank lower among the supplied specific issues in both views. [billing--premium-upgrade-mentions:rank] [sample:billing--premium-upgrade-mentions:rank]
original_memo.limitations: Coverage is partial: the supplied claims show completed rows against a larger set of nonempty rows, and a substantial share of complaint rows is unspecified. These limitations mean the classified issue mix should not be read as a complete account of all feedback. [scope:completed_rows] [scope:nonempty_rows] [scope:coverage_percent] [scope:complaint_rows] [scope:unspecified_complaint_rows] [scope:unspecified_percent] The ranking may be affected by duplicate-text weighting and uncertain lexical cohorts; classifier errors are preserved rather than corrected. Verifier and fallback results may be correlated. Complaints expressing cancellation are not evidence of observed churn, and failed-call usage is unknown. Before-checkpoint provenance is reconstructed, not independently established. These constraints preclude causal, revenue, or churn estimates.
original_memo.random_prefix_comparison: The random-prefix-only ranking also places free-tier playback controls locked behind Premium above the other specific actionable issues. It differs in ordering the next two: unspecified usability complaints precede intrusive advertisements in that ranking, whereas advertisements precede unspecified usability in the baseline. The broad no-stated-cause bucket remains first in both rankings, but is not an actionable recommendation. [sample:cross-topic--free-tier-premium-controls:rank] [sample:usability--unspecified:rank] [sample:usability--ad-interruptions:rank] [cross-topic--free-tier-premium-controls:rank] [usability--ad-interruptions:rank] [usability--unspecified:rank] [sample:other--unspecified:rank] [other--unspecified:rank]
original_memo.recommendation: Prioritize investigating free-tier playback controls locked behind Premium, the top specific actionable issue. It ranks ahead of the other specific issues in the baseline, with a higher severity-weighted priority score than intrusive advertisements, unspecified usability complaints, or premium-upgrade mentions. [cross-topic--free-tier-premium-controls:rank] [cross-topic--free-tier-premium-controls:priority_score] [usability--ad-interruptions:priority_score] [usability--unspecified:priority_score] [billing--premium-upgrade-mentions:priority_score]
original_memo.top_bucket_explanation: The largest bucket is general dissatisfaction with no stated cause, not a specific actionable defect. Its prominence describes an unclassified complaint, so it should not be treated as a product fix. [other--unspecified:complaint_count] [other--unspecified:rank]

verifier.interpretation: Blinded Luna agreement, not human accuracy; fallback also uses Luna. Duplicate texts induce dependence. Entities excluded.
